claims.statement: In Poland, an electronic CMR that satisfies the Additional Protocol has the same evidentiary value and effect as a paper CMR, but it requires reliable authentication, integrity, authorized-party access and agreed issuance, delivery-confirmation and amendment procedures.

From 9 July 2027 authorities must accept regulatory freight information supplied through certified eFTI platforms; operators remain free to use paper, while electronic submissions to authorities must use certified eFTI infrastructure.
Polish-registered vehicles performed 368 billion tonne-kilometres in 2024, nearly 20% of EU road freight activity, confirming a large and recurrent underlying shipment base.

One Poland-focused forwarder's published terms start a default 45-day payment period only after the invoice and complete CMR/POD set are uploaded, permit payment withholding for damage questions and penalize late document delivery.
Factris says a transport invoice needs confirmed delivery such as a CMR receipt, funds can arrive within one working day after complete documentation and advances can reach 90% of invoice value.

Dashdoc already connects eCMR, delivery evidence and invoicing, while Transporeon already validates freight invoices through payment-ready verification and manages disputes inside its transport platform.

Dashdoc's 2026 market guide places transport SaaS around EUR 50-150 per user or EUR 30-80 per vehicle monthly plus setup, which is a budget anchor but not evidence that buyers will pay separately for a readiness sidecar.

The EU Payment Observatory reported that more than half of companies experienced late-payment difficulties in 2024 and average B2B and government-to-business payment periods exceeded 60 days, but this does not isolate document defects as the cause.

contrary_evidence: Dashdoc already joins eCMR, attachments, signatures and immediate invoicing, directly overlapping document capture and carrier workflow.
Transporeon already provides platform-native freight audit, payment-ready verification and dispute management, giving a large incumbent structural data and distribution advantages.
Factris already accepts a CMR receipt as delivery proof and may improve its own rules rather than buy an external document-readiness module.
EU-wide late-payment evidence establishes cash-flow pain but not the share caused by missing or contradictory freight documents.
eFTI certification is required for electronic regulatory submissions to authorities, so the product must remain outside that submission role.
Published TMS pricing validates broader software budgets, not willingness to pay for a paid backtest, implementation, recurring minimum or per-packet factor module.

No reviewed source establishes that a factor will buy the backtest, grant production data access, accept an external document-completeness gate, commit recurring volume or permit reuse of outcome labels.

economics.acquisition_route: Sell one bounded paid backtest directly to a factor operations and risk sponsor using its permissioned historical export. Do not fund production connectors, carrier acquisition or a marketplace listing before the factor signs access terms, paid implementation and a recurring minimum; the enterprise sales cycle and conversion remain unknown.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: No evidence-backed path can yet be calculated. A path to 5m PLN of founder net worth would require multiple factors renewing at positive contribution after implementation and support, with account value, sales cycle, churn, owner earnings and valuation measured rather than inferred. The redesign makes those variables testable and removes the prior unsupported shipment-volume forecast; it does not establish the outcome.
economics.founder_time: Cap unpaid validation and the paid backtest at 15-20 hours weekly. Production begins only if contract revenue supports external legal, security and integration capacity; abandon the structure if recurring exception handling remains founder-bound or exceeds the founder's five-hour daily ceiling.
economics.gross_margin_basis: The backtest and implementation are service-heavy, and no margin is assumed. The production monthly minimum must cover factor-specific mapping, security, support and contracted operations before per-packet revenue counts as contribution; measured straight-through clearance and exception labor determine whether software-like margins exist.
economics.payback: Unknown until the sales cycle, paid-backtest effort, implementation cost, exception labor and renewal are measured. Paid discovery makes the first account non-free and reduces speculative integration cash exposure, but it does not prove acquisition payback; expansion requires positive account-level cash contribution.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated contract architecture, not an asserted market price: a paid fixed-scope backtest and separately paid implementation, followed by a monthly minimum sized to dedicated mapping and support plus a per-processed-packet charge, with no success or funding guarantee. Exact amounts must be learned in the first procurement process.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each pre-funding document review is a repeated event, and factor-specific rule versions, evidence trails and operational history can create workflow switching cost. Renewal is unproven, a minimum term is not product validation, and the factor or an incumbent can still internalize the module.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable source-connector templates, a transport-document ontology, versioned rule and audit tooling, and exception-operations playbooks can reduce the marginal work of later factor deployments. Client rejection or cure outcomes contribute to cross-client learning only where contract and law expressly permit, so no ungranted data moat is assumed.
fingerprint.customer: Regional Polish and Central European transport-invoice factors whose operations teams manually reconcile carrier invoices, orders and CMR/POD packets before deciding whether documentation is ready for funding
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: A direct contract-first sale to one factor's operations and risk sponsor: run only a paid, fixed-scope backtest on permissioned historical packets, and undertake production integration only after processor terms, access scope and a recurring minimum are contracted. No carrier-by-carrier acquisition or TMS marketplace placement is assumed.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A factor-specific document-readiness decision cell: rules-as-code, cross-source reconciliation, versioned evidence trails and exception routing, initially fed by permissioned batch exports or uploads rather than speculative deep integrations. It is sold as a paid backtest and implementation followed by a monthly minimum and per-processed-packet charge; the factor retains the final funding and legal decisions.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The factor pays for a fixed-scope historical backtest and implementation, then a contracted monthly minimum plus usage for packets processed through its document-readiness gate; production begins only after authorized access and the recurring minimum are signed.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A factor's operations queue receives completed-transport invoices from heterogeneous carrier, TMS and eCMR sources, but staff must manually test each packet against the factor's documented pre-funding evidence rules and cure exceptions before the funding decision can proceed.

founder_fit: Rules-as-code, document extraction, entity matching, audit trails and exception measurement fit the founder's data-science and AI leverage.
A 40,000 PLN pre-production capital cap and paid implementation gate limit speculative exposure; production legal, security and connector work must be funded and delegated.
The model avoids carrier-by-carrier selling and public-facing content, but winning a factor sponsor remains a concentrated enterprise sale that may strain the founder's social energy.
The construction remains part-time only while the backtest is bounded and recurring exceptions are handled by contracted operators rather than the founder.

redesign.economic_effect: Moves the venture from an optional sidecar that speculatively needs partner access and distribution to a contract-first factor operations module: the same buyer pays for the backtest and implementation, signs access and a recurring minimum before production, and supplies repeated portfolio workflow. This caps pre-production founder capital at 40,000 PLN, makes customization funded rather than sunk and removes carrier-by-carrier acquisition from the model. It does not prove demand or margins: if no factor accepts those terms, development stops, and reusable economics still depend on measured exception labor and reuse of connector and rule tooling.

risks: Calling the module a decision cell could be mistaken for a guarantee of authenticity, collectability, legal entitlement or funding; contracts and interfaces must leave every such decision with the factor.
Electronic CMR validity depends on authentication, integrity, authorized access and agreed procedures that a reconciled upload alone may not establish.
Factor and carrier packets contain personal and commercially sensitive information, requiring scoped authorization, processor terms, access controls, retention rules and audit logs.
The paid backtest may not convert, and no production work should begin merely to rescue sunk sales effort.
One anchor factor creates customer concentration and can demand bespoke rules, restrict reusable learnings or internalize the feature.
Custom mappings and manual exceptions can erase the monthly minimum's contribution and make later deployments repeated services projects.
Dashdoc, Transporeon or the factor's own team can bundle the same readiness logic while controlling the source workflow.
Direct enterprise procurement and ongoing sponsor management may exceed the founder's part-time or social-energy constraints.

structure.commercial_archetype: Contract-first vertical operations infrastructure: paid diagnostic and implementation followed by minimum-commitment usage software for a transport-invoice factor
structure.control_point: The factor-configured document-completeness gate inside its pre-funding operations queue, while the factor retains the financial decision
structure.critical_dependency: A factor must pay for a bounded historical backtest and then sign authorized data access, processor terms and a recurring minimum before production work; absent that evidence, the candidate stops with limited sunk cost.

thesis: Sell a bounded paid historical backtest and then a contract-gated production module directly to a transport-invoice factor, rather than building a generic carrier-facing readiness score or relying on a TMS marketplace. The factor supplies authorized sample packets and its own documented completeness rules; the module reconciles invoice, order and existing CMR/POD evidence from batch exports or uploads, preserves the source trail and routes exceptions at the factor's pre-funding document gate. Production work begins only after paid implementation, processor and access terms, and a recurring minimum are signed. The factor retains every credit, collectability, authenticity, liability and final funding decision, and the module neither creates an eCMR nor acts as an eFTI platform. This construction makes the concentrated partner dependency a paid pass/fail procurement gate and funds customization before scale, but no reviewed evidence establishes that a factor will accept these terms.
title: Contract-First Factor Document-Readiness Decision Cell
uncertainties: Whether a factor will pay for the bounded historical backtest rather than evaluate the workflow internally
Baseline share and monetary value of funding queues blocked specifically by correctable document defects
Whether a factor will sign authorized access, processor terms, paid implementation and a recurring minimum
Straight-through clearance, false-positive and false-negative cost, and manual minutes per exception on real factor packets
How much source mapping and rule configuration can be reused across factors, country pairs and document systems
Exact contract value, sales cycle, implementation cost, account contribution, renewal and churn
Whether factor-specific rules and audit history create enough switching cost before an incumbent bundles equivalent capability
Whether any partner expressly permits lawful reuse of de-identified rejection and cure outcomes
Whether legal and product controls reliably keep the module outside authenticity, collectability, liability, final funding and eFTI-platform decisions
